intent.summary: Restore the original request path for Vercel ISR invocations so ISR pages render instead of returning 404. The PR reports this as a regression from #15959 and says manual Vercel end-to-end tests observed successful rendering after the rewrite.

findings.title: ISR path rewrite exposes its internal path query parameter to Astro routes
findings.suggested_fix: After reading the ISR path, delete ASTRO_PATH_PARAM from url.searchParams before rebuilding the Request, preserving all other query parameters.
findings.why_it_matters: The handler uses x_astro_path to restore the route pathname, then rebuilds the Request without removing that internal parameter. Astro normalizes request.url for page rendering, so ISR pages receive x_astro_path as an ordinary query parameter; pages that inspect query parameters or build URLs from them can observe adapter routing state.
evidence: packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts:27-33 -- the URL pathname is replaced and the request is rebuilt while url.searchParams remains intact

testing_gaps.title: ISR request rewriting has no runtime test
testing_gaps.why_it_matters: The existing ISR tests verify generated routes and prerender configuration but never invoke the generated handler with an ISR request. They would not catch regressions in restoration of the original path or leakage of the internal query parameter.
testing_gaps.suggested_fix: Add a runtime test that invokes the generated _isr handler with x-vercel-isr: 1 and x_astro_path for an ISR route, then checks the rendered route and Astro-visible query parameters.
evidence: packages/integrations/vercel/test/isr.test.js:16 -- test only checks generated prerender config
